title: The twelfth week
subtitle: Three months. The hardest stretch is behind you, and the next stage starts next week.

baby.development: Your baby is laughing, babbling, and may be rolling. They can see across a room and are starting to reach for what they want.

you.body: Bleeding is long finished. Your core and pelvic floor are still healing, and they will keep healing for a year. Your hair is shedding and will stop.
you.mind: The end of the fourth trimester is a real milestone and it is worth noticing. If you have been waiting to feel better before asking for help, this is the week to stop waiting.

coreActions.title: Book the four-month visit
coreActions.why: The four-month visit is the next vaccine set and the next developmental check, and the good slots go early.
coreActions.detail: Ask about rolling, head shape, and sleep. Ask whether the baby is ready for solids yet, which is usually a conversation for the six-month visit. Bring the mood screening up if it has not been asked.

coreActions.title: Keep tummy time going, every day
coreActions.why: Tummy time is still the best thing for the strength that comes before sitting and crawling.
coreActions.detail: Aim for twenty to thirty minutes a day in short bursts. Get down at eye level with a toy or a mirror. A baby who can push up on straight arms is getting close to rolling.

coreActions.title: Decide what support you want for the next year
coreActions.why: The first year is long, and the support that got you through the first three months is not the support you need for the next nine.
coreActions.detail: A therapist, a parent group, a weekly call with a friend, or childcare one morning a week. Pick one thing and put it in the calendar. The maternal mental health line is free if you want to talk to someone first.

alsoKnow.title: Solids are still a few months away
alsoKnow.body: Most babies are ready around six months, when they can sit with support and hold their head steady. Starting earlier does not help sleep and does not help allergies.

alsoKnow.title: Teeth may be close
alsoKnow.body: First teeth usually arrive between four and seven months. Drool and chewing on hands start earlier and are not a sign that a tooth is imminent.

redFlags.text: A fever of 100.4°F or higher in a baby under three months
Fast or labored breathing, or a blue tint around the lips
Feeling hopeless most of the day, or thoughts of harming yourself or the baby
